title: Discrete Diffusion Modeling by Estimating the Ratios of the Data Distribution

nodes.text: Score entropy is a novel loss function that extends score matching to discrete spaces by learning the concrete score (ratios of the data distribution p(y)/p(x)), built off a Bregman divergence with F = -log rather than the Fisher divergence used in standard score matching.
nodes.evidence: we bridge this gap by proposing score entropy, a novel loss that naturally extends score matching to discrete spaces

nodes.text: Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion (SEDD) parameterizes a reverse discrete diffusion process by directly estimating the ratios of the data distribution (the concrete score), learned via score entropy.
nodes.evidence: SEDD parameterizes a reverse discrete diffusion process using the ratios of the data distribution. These are learned using score entropy

nodes.text: The concrete score (ratios pt(y)/pt(x)) generalizes the typical score function ∇x log pt used in continuous score-based diffusion models, making score entropy analogous to score matching.
nodes.evidence: the ratios pt(y)/pt(x) (which are collectively known as the concrete score ... generalizing the typical score function ∇x log pt

nodes.text: Score entropy improves upon Concrete Score Matching (Meng et al. 2022), whose l2 loss is incompatible with the positivity of the ratios and fails to penalize negative/zero values, leading to divergent behavior; score entropy instead rescales problematic gradients to form a natural log-barrier keeping scores nonnegative.
nodes.evidence: the l2 loss is incompatible with the fact that pt(y)/pt(x) must be positive ... score entropy directly improves upon concrete score matching by rescaling problematic gradients

nodes.text: Mean prediction approaches (Austin et al. 2021; Campbell et al. 2022) that learn the reverse density p0|t recover the ratios only in a roundabout way and underperform, since learning a density is harder and the objective breaks down in continuous time and must be approximated.
nodes.evidence: learning p0|t is inherently harder since it is a density ... the objective breaks down in continuous time and must be approximated ... this framework largely underperforms empirically

nodes.text: Ratio matching (Hyvarinen 2007; Sun et al. 2023) departs from standard score matching and requires specialized, expensive network architectures, tending to perform worse than mean prediction.
nodes.evidence: the resulting setup departs from standard score matching and requires specialized and expensive network architectures ... tends to perform worse than mean prediction

nodes.text: Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion challenges the longstanding dominance of autoregressive models, which had been the only competitive method for discrete data such as natural language for decades.
nodes.evidence: we challenge the longstanding dominance of autoregressive models ... autoregressive modeling ... has remained the only competitive method for decades

nodes.text: Denoising Score Entropy (DSE) is a scalable variant of score entropy, analogous to denoising score matching (Vincent 2011), which only requires evaluating a single score network output per Monte Carlo sample and replaces the unknown ratios with tractable diffusion transition densities.
nodes.evidence: we work a denoising score matching loss (Vincent, 2011) variant of score entropy ... LDSE is scalable since Monte Carlo sampling only requires the evaluation of one sθ(x)

nodes.text: The Diffusion Weighted Denoising Score Entropy (DWDSE) yields an ELBO that upper-bounds the negative log-likelihood, enabling likelihood-based training and evaluation (and perplexity) for discrete diffusion models, with the implicit version coinciding with the likelihood loss of Campbell et al. (2022).
nodes.evidence: the score entropy can be used to define an ELBO for likelihood-based training ... the implicit version coincides with the likelihood loss introduced in Campbell et al. (2022)

nodes.text: Tweedie tau-leaping is a sampling strategy that generalizes the discrete Tweedie's theorem to optimally denoise: it minimizes the KL divergence with the true reverse process among all tau-leaping strategies when the score is learned perfectly.
nodes.evidence: Theorem 4.2 (Tweedie τ-leaping) ... this minimizes the KL divergence with the true reverse pt−∆t|t ... for all τ-leaping strategies

nodes.text: On standard language modeling tasks at comparable model sizes, SEDD reduces perplexity by 25-75% relative to existing language diffusion paradigms and is competitive with autoregressive models, beating GPT-2 on its zero-shot perplexity tasks.
nodes.evidence: SEDD beats existing language diffusion paradigms (reducing perplexity by 25-75%) and is competitive with autoregressive models, in particular outperforming GPT-2

nodes.text: SEDD generates faithful unconditional text without distribution annealing (e.g. temperature scaling/nucleus sampling), achieving around 6-8x (up to 68x for un-annealed GPT-2) better generative perplexity than similarly sized GPT-2.
nodes.evidence: around 68× better generative perplexity than un-annealed GPT-2 ... SEDD beats GPT-2 by 6-8×

nodes.text: SEDD can trade compute for quality, matching sample quality while using 32x fewer network function evaluations.
nodes.evidence: can trade compute and quality (similar quality with 32× fewer network evaluations)

nodes.text: By directly parameterizing probability ratios, SEDD enables controllable infilling and prompting from arbitrary positions without specialized training, matching nucleus-sampling quality (by MAUVE score) while supporting strategies beyond left-to-right generation.
nodes.evidence: one can prompt SEDD from arbitrary positions without specialized training ... comparable with autoregressive models with nucleus sampling (as measured by MAUVE score

nodes.text: For high-dimensional sequence tasks, SEDD uses a sparse structured token-level transition matrix (uniform or absorbing/MASK state, the latter akin to BERT) so only Hamming-distance-1 ratios need modeling, giving training speed and memory comparable to standard autoregressive training.
nodes.evidence: we instead choose a sparse structured matrix that perturbs tokens independently ... our training iteration is about as fast and uses a similar amount of memory as standard autoregressive training
